mechanism_narrative: Sustained negative WORKPLACES mobility (-15.1% at t-0w) signals continued remote work adoption. This reduces weekday commuting-adjacent retail visits, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -12.3% to -15.1% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days by more than 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has collapsed to -38.6% at t-0w, indicating suppressed outdoor leisure activity. This behavioral shift redirects discretionary spending away from outdoor recreation venues toward indoor retail, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks as substitution occurs.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -35% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -38.6% in t-0w, -37.3% in t-2w
regime_hint: heat wave or weather-driven outdoor avoidance
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase week-on-week in at least 2 of the next 3 weeks following the trigger condition.

regime_hint: transit-dependent urban area under mobility restrictions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points over the next 28 days despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remaining below trigger thresholds.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains negative or declines further over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining positive.

This regime persists, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next week as the behavioral pattern locks in.
